items.content_excerpt: $ONDS IF you are a long, do you know what you own? You own a cash-burning, acquisition driven roll-up whose underlying economics are pathetically weak. Q3 delivered a $189.5 million operating LOSS and a widened $59.7 million adjusted EBITDA loss. GAAP gross margins collapsed to 21.8%. The deceptive growth is heavily inorganic. Worthless goodwill on the books continues to mask the fact that this company way overpaid for most of their acquisitions. Massive dilution. Share count has ballooned dramatically to 590 million. Stock-based compensation and other non-cash items remains substantial. Investors see continued dilution, margin pressure, and execution risk. What about that $835 million backlog? NO ONE CARES. IT’S NOT RECOGNIZED REVENUE. In short, the financial picture is bad with spending heavily to buy revenue while GAAP profitability is a long…long way off. Finally, with Democrats assuming power everywhere, the poltical landscape is bearish for defence contractors.

items.title: $APLD more big progress in Louisiana at Delta Forge One toward public financing of the $META AI factory’s construction $APLD moved another s
items.content_excerpt: $APLD more big progress in Louisiana at Delta Forge One toward public financing of the $META AI factory’s construction $APLD moved another step forward in Louisiana. KALB reports today that the England Authority unanimously voted November 9 to introduce the PILOT agreement for Delta Forge 1, the planned 300-megawatt campus, with final approval possible November 19 - one week from today. The PILOT arrangement, meaning payments in lieu of taxes, anticipates up to $575.5 million for local taxing bodies over its full term, plus a separate $50 million community benefit trust. Here is how this connects to the proposed $4.6 billion in bonds: the same document combines the PILOT tax arrangement with an optional bond-financing framework. The authority would hold title to the property and lease it back to $APLD’s project subsidiary, providing property-tax relief in exchange for negotiated payments. A separate provision would allow the authority, at the subsidiary’s request, to issue up to $4.6 billion in revenue bonds to finance data-center buildings, power infrastructure and cooling. (englandairpark.org⁠￼) The authority would issue those bonds, while $APLD’s project subsidiary would make the payments needed to repay bondholders. The authority’s general funds would not back the debt. Before issuance, the subsidiary would need to identify a buyer or underwriter, establish financing terms and collateral, and satisfy additional requirements, including Louisiana State Bond Commission approval. The $4.6 billion is a borrowing ceiling under the proposed agreement and it does not establish that investors committed that money or that $APLD received it. (englandairpark.org⁠￼) For my own investment in $APLD, I see progress on the local tax agreement and a potential financing option. The draft expressly preserves the tax incentives even if no bonds are issued. The Town Talk also reported November 10 that Louisiana Central attorney Mike Busada said there was no current plan to issue bonds. November 19 could therefore advance the agreement, while an actual bond sale and funding would remain separate milestones. (englandairpark.org⁠￼, aol.com⁠￼) Sources: KALB, November 12: https://www.kalb.com/2026/11/12/england-authority-sets-stage-final-vote-applied-digital-data-center-pilot-agreement/⁠￼ Official proposed agreement, Section 3.03, PDF pages 20–21: https://englandairpark.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/1.1a-Notice-and-Agenda-11.9.2026.pdf⁠￼ The Town Talk, November 10, republished by AOL: https://www.aol.com/articles/transformational-england-commissioners-discuss-data-150227000.html⁠￼

items.title: $ANT $NVDA $AMD $AVGO The timing of Jensen Huang's downfall is getting extremely suspicious. Rumors are growing around Nvidia, Anthropic
items.content_excerpt: $ANT $NVDA $AMD $AVGO The timing of Jensen Huang's downfall is getting extremely suspicious. Rumors are growing around Nvidia, Anthropic, and a very strange series of events that ended with Jensen Huang losing his CEO position. And the most interesting part is that this story didn't start in October. It started 4 years ago when Jensen Huang met Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei for dinner. The meeting reportedly turned into a heated argument over AI chips, with Anthropic's team claiming Google's chips offered better value than NVIDIA's. Amodei even reportedly compared Huang to Donald Trump, and then things got worse. In June 2025, Huang publicly said he disagreed with almost everything Amodei said about AI. Amodei fired back, accusing Huang of lying about his views. They were also on opposite sides of a major debate over China. Huang wanted Nvidia to keep competing in the Chinese market, while Amodei pushed for tighter restrictions on advanced AI chip exports. Despite all that, NVIDIA agreed to invest up to $10 Billion in Anthropic, but here's where the timeline gets interesting. In October 2025, a company linked to Alice Huang (an alleged Chinese spy) came under investigation over suspected chip-export violations. By late 2025, Trump had reportedly been briefed about intelligence concerns involving Alice Huang and Jensen Huang but took no action. And the alleged intelligence connection didn't become a major public story for months. Then, almost a year later, everything happened within just 17 days. • October 26: Anthropic filed for its massive IPO. • October 29: The alleged Chinese intelligence connection involving Jensen Huang became public. • November 8: Huang admitted to an extramarital relationship. • November 10: Anthropic filed an amended IPO prospectus. • November 12: Huang resigned, and NVIDIA shares plunged. Think about what just happened. The concerns had reportedly been known inside the US government for months. But the public scandal broke 3 days after Anthropic's IPO filing. And less than two weeks later, one of the most powerful men in AI was no longer running Nvidia. Now Anthropic is preparing for a massive IPO while Nvidia faces a leadership crisis. Huang's departure could potentially give Anthropic more negotiating power, encourage companies to move toward alternative AI chips, and reduce the influence of a powerful opponent of Amodei's position on China. Of course, Nvidia is also an investor in Anthropic, so a broader AI crash could hurt its IPO. None of this means that Anthropic or Amodei had any role in Huang's scandal, but the timing is fascinating.

items.content_excerpt: $SMMT Mizuho analyst: SMMT’s Ivonescimab could become a major cancer-treatment platform On November 2, BioSpace published an interview with Graig Suvannavejh, senior biotech analyst at Mizuho. His assessment was particularly optimistic. He believes ivonescimab has the potential to become a foundational treatment that physicians combine with other cancer drugs. His argument is based on more than one successful clinical trial. He points to the growing number of pharmaceutical companies interested in combining their experimental therapies with SMMT’s ivonescimab. These include AstraZeneca, Pfizer⁠ and Revolution Medicines⁠. The important distinction is that these companies aren’t simply betting on one lung cancer indication. They’re investigating whether ivonescimab could improve treatment across multiple cancers. https://www.biospace.com/drug-development/drugmakers-rush-to-pair-up-with-summits-ivonescimab-ahead-of-key-verdict

The authority would hold title to the property and lease it back to $APLD’s project subsidiary, providing property-tax relief in exchange for negotiated payments. A separate provision would allow the authority, at the subsidiary’s request, to issue up to $4.6 billion in revenue bonds to finance data-center buildings, power infrastructure and cooling. (englandairpark.org⁠￼) The authority would issue those bonds, while $APLD’s project subsidiary would make the payments needed to repay bondholders. The authority’s general funds would not back the debt. Before issuance, the subsidiary would need to identify a buyer or underwriter, establish financing terms and collateral, and satisfy additional requirements, including Louisiana State Bond Commission approval. The $4.6 billion is a borrowing ceiling under the proposed agreement and it does not establish that investors committed that money or that $APLD received it. $ANT $NVDA $AMD $AVGO The timing of Jensen Huang's downfall is getting extremely suspicious. Rumors are growing around Nvidia, Anthropic, and a very strange series of events that ended with Jensen Huang losing his CEO position. And the most interesting part is that this story didn't start in October. It started 4 years ago when Jensen Huang met Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei for dinner. The meeting reportedly turned into a heated argument over AI chips, with Anthropic's team claiming Google's chips offered better value than NVIDIA's. Amodei even reportedly compared Huang to Donald Trump, and then things got worse. In June 2025, Huang publicly said he disagreed with almost everything Amodei said about AI. Amodei fired back, accusing Huang of lying about his views. They were also on opposite sides of a major debate over China. Huang wanted Nvidia to keep competing in the Chinese market, while Amodei pushed for tighter restrictions on advanced AI chip exports. Despite all that, NVIDIA agreed to invest up to $10 Billion in Anthropic, but here's where the timeline gets interesting. In October 2025, a company linked to Alice Huang (an alleged Chinese spy) came under investigation over suspected chip-export violations. By late 2025, Trump had reportedly been briefed about intelligence concerns involving Alice Huang and Jensen Huang but took no action. And the alleged intelligence connection didn't become a major public story for months. Then, almost a year later, everything happened within just 17 days. • October 26: Anthropic filed for its massive IPO. • October 29: The alleged Chinese intelligence connection involving Jensen Huang became public. • November 8: Huang admitted to an extramarital relationship. • November 10: Anthropic filed an amended IPO prospectus. • November 12: Huang resigned, and NVIDIA shares plunged. Think about what just happened. The concerns had reportedly been known inside the US government for months. But the public scandal broke 3 days after Anthropic's IPO filing. And less than two weeks later, one of the most powerful men in AI was no longer running Nvidia. Now Anthropic is preparing for a massive IPO while Nvidia faces a leadership crisis. Huang's departure could potentially give Anthropic more negotiating power, encourage companies to move toward alternative AI chips, and reduce the influence of a powerful opponent of Amodei's position on China. Of course, Nvidia is also an investor in Anthropic, so a broader AI crash could hurt its IPO. None of this means that Anthropic or Amodei had any role in Huang's scandal, but the timing is fascinating.
